summary: Children read and write time to the exact minute on analogue and digital clocks. The efficient method is not counting single minutes from the 12 but finding the last 5-minute interval the minute hand has passed and counting on (e.g. 23 past = 4×5 = 20, then +3). 'To' times add a conversion step: turning minutes-past into minutes-to the next hour using a number bond to 60 (44 past 3 = 16 to 4). The hour hand also needs care: late in the hour it moves close to the next numeral, but the hour is the number it has LAST passed (at 7:43 the hour hand is about three-quarters of the way to 8, but the hour is still 7; at 9:57 it is almost on 10, but the hour is still 9).
misconceptions: Counts individual minutes from 12 to the hand instead of counting on from the nearest 5 below (slow and error-prone)
Multi-step 'minutes to' reading breaks down (miscounts the bond to 60)
Reads the hour as the numeral the hour hand is nearest, so 7:43 becomes '8:43' (hour hand almost on 8)
Reads a digital time literally rather than converting it (says 'seven forty-three' but can't render it on analogue or as a 'to' time)

activities.title: Count on from the last five on a moveable clock
steps: On a clock with moveable hands and a minute scale (tick marks), set the minute hand to a target such as 43 minutes.
Find the last 5-minute mark the hand has passed (40) by counting the fives: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40.
Count on the extra single minutes from there: 41, 42, 43 — do not count all 43 ticks one at a time from the 12.
Check the hour hand: notice it has moved about three-quarters of the way toward the next numeral, and say the hour as the number it has LAST passed.
Try another near-the-hour example: set 9:57 — the hour hand is almost on 10, but the hour is still 9 because that is the number it has last passed.
Read the whole time aloud (e.g. 'forty-three minutes past seven' / 'seven forty-three').
activities.insight: The quick, reliable way to read exact minutes is to land on the nearest 5-minute mark below the hand and count on the remaining minutes, and to read the hour as the numeral the hour hand has last passed.

activities.title: Convert 'past' to 'minutes to' with a bond to 60
steps: Start from an exact 'past' reading such as 43 minutes past 7.
On a number line from 0 to 60 (or a part-whole bond), find how far it is from 43 up to 60: 43 + 17 = 60.
State the 'to' time: 43 past 7 is 17 minutes to 8.
Repeat with other examples, e.g. 44 past 3 = 16 to 4; 57 past 9 = 3 to 10.
Say both forms of the same time aloud to connect them.
activities.insight: Reading a 'to' time is one extra step on top of reading the 'past' time: use a number bond to 60 to find the gap to the next hour, and remember the hour named is the NEXT hour.

activities.title: Match and write analogue and digital to the exact minute, both directions
steps: Read an analogue clock set to 7:43 and write it as a digital time.
Given a digital time such as 11:06, set the hands: minute hand just past the 1 (at the 6-minute tick), hour hand just past the 11.
Match several analogue faces to their digital equivalents to the exact minute.
For each, say the hour it has last passed and the minutes found by counting on.
Answer targeted checks, e.g. 'The hour hand is almost on 8 — what is the hour?' and 'Fill in: 44 minutes past 3 = ___ minutes to 4.'
activities.insight: Exact-minute times can be translated faithfully between analogue and digital in both directions, keeping the count-on method and the last-passed hour.

checkQuestion: Set exact-minute reading and writing tasks and WATCH the method: (1) Analogue clock set to 7:43 with the hour hand nearly on 8: 'Read this time to me — tell me the hour and the minutes — and show me how you work out the minutes.' (2) 'Now write it as a digital time.' (3) Give a digital 11:06: 'Set these hands on the clock.' Watch whether they count on from the last five (40, then 41-42-43) or count single minutes from the 12, and whether they keep the hour at 7 (not 8).
checkAnswer: Finds the last 5-minute mark (40) and counts on 3 to reach 43; reads the hour as 7 (the number the hour hand has last passed); writes 7:43; sets 11:06 with the minute hand just past the 1 and the hour hand just past the 11.
